scenes.heading: Inheritance and Punnett squares
scenes.sub: How can two brown-eyed parents have a blue-eyed child?
scenes.say: Why can two brown-eyed parents have a blue-eyed child? Gregor Mendel worked out the rules with pea plants in the eighteen hundreds. A simple grid called a Punnett square lets you use them.
scenes.caption: Why can two brown-eyed parents have a blue-eyed child? Gregor Mendel worked out the rules with pea plants in the 1800s. A simple grid called a Punnett square lets you use them.

scenes.heading: Genotype vs phenotype
scenes.say: Your genotype is the pair of alleles you carry, like big T little t. Your phenotype is the characteristic that shows, like being tall. It's like an app's code versus what you see on screen.
scenes.caption: Your genotype is the pair of alleles you carry, like Tt. Your phenotype is the characteristic that shows, like being tall. It's like an app's code versus what you see on screen.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: A loud speaker drowns out a quiet one
scenes.science: A dominant allele hides a recessive one
scenes.breaks: a quiet speaker still makes some sound, but a recessive allele doesn't show at all. And dominant doesn't mean more common or better.
scenes.say: A dominant allele is like a loud speaker: one copy is enough to show. A recessive allele only shows with two copies. A heterozygous person, big T little t, is a carrier: they don't show the trait, but can pass it on.
scenes.caption: A dominant allele is like a loud speaker: one copy is enough to show. A recessive allele only shows with two copies. A heterozygous person, Tt, is a carrier: they don't show the trait, but can pass it on.

scenes.heading: Making a Punnett square
steps: Put them along the top and side
scenes.say: Each gamete gets just one allele. That's Mendel's law of segregation. Write the parents' genotypes and their gametes, put them along the top and side, fill each box, then count the ratios.

scenes.heading: Carrier parents
scenes.question: Cystic fibrosis is recessive (f). Both parents are carriers (Ff). What are the chances for each child?
lines: Gametes from each parent: F or f
scenes.say: Cystic fibrosis is caused by a recessive allele. If both parents are carriers, one box in four has two recessive alleles, and two boxes have one of each. So each child has a twenty-five percent chance of cystic fibrosis and a fifty percent chance of being a carrier.
scenes.caption: Cystic fibrosis is caused by a recessive allele. If both parents are carriers, one box in four has two recessive alleles (ff), and two boxes have one of each (Ff). So each child has a 25% chance of cystic fibrosis and a 50% chance of being a carrier.

scenes.heading: Three key crosses
points: Each child is a fresh coin toss
scenes.say: Learn the three key crosses. Two heterozygous parents give a three to one ratio. Heterozygous with homozygous recessive gives one to one. Homozygous dominant with recessive gives all dominant. And each child is a fresh coin toss.

scenes.heading: X-linked traits
points: Some genes are on the X, not the Y
So recessive X-linked traits show more in males
scenes.say: Some genes, like the one for red–green colour blindness, are on the X chromosome but not the Y. Boys have no backup X, so a single recessive allele shows. That's why colour blindness is much more common in males.

points: X-linked recessive: more common in males
scenes.say: Quick recap. Genotype is the alleles, phenotype is what shows. Dominant alleles need one copy, recessive need two. Punnett squares give probabilities for each child. Now try the practice questions!
